model: BVPS compounding x exit P/B (holdco/insurer route, not owner-FCF)

inputs.share_count_date: 2026-09-26 (approx, cross-checked market cap / price vs stockanalysis.com reported shares outstanding)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 7.5-10% across scenarios reflects a AAA-quality, permanent-capital diversified conglomerate: lower than a typical small/mid-cap discount rate given no leverage risk, no refinancing risk, and float-funded rather than debt-funded capital structure. Base case 8.5% sits near a long-run US equity cost of capital for a low-beta mega-cap.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: Berkshire is an insurer/holdco/compounder-of-book per the dcf-methods routing table -- NOT an owner-FCF DCF. Berkshire's reported operating cash flow and FCF are not owner earnings: they are swamped by the ~$300-400B T-bill/cash pile's placement, insurance float mechanics, and a large marketable-securities portfolio subject to mandatory mark-to-market GAAP swings (net income swung from -$22.8B in FY2022 to +$97.1B in FY2023 on investment marks alone, unrelated to operating performance). FCF/WACC on this business would double-count value already sitting in the equity portfolio and would need to model float as debt, which it is not. Instead this model compounds book value per share (BVPS) -- the metric Berkshire's own historical shareholder letters used before discontinuing per-share intrinsic-value commentary -- forward at a scenario growth rate, and capitalizes the terminal BVPS at an exit price-to-book multiple drawn from Berkshire's own recent trading range (~1.1x buyback-comfort floor per Q1 2026 management commentary, up to ~1.6x in strong markets), discounted at a cost of equity appropriate for a AAA-quality permanent-capital conglomerate. No dividend is paid (confirmed zero DPS every period in core_metrics) so all scenario value is in the terminal BVPS x exit-P/B leg; there is no interim FCF or dividend stream to add. SHARES OUTSTANDING GAP: SEC XBRL structured tags (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, WeightedAverageNumberOfSharesOutstandingBasic) are NULL or wrongly-dimensioned for BRK-B in every period in core_metrics after ~2011 -- confirmed by direct query of the SEC companyconcept API, which shows the tag reporting ~940K-1.1M 'shares' in 2010-2011, consistent with Class-A-only counts on a filer that also has a 1500x-smaller Class B share class; Berkshire's own filings mix Class A and B-equivalent counts inconsistently across tag versions, and no clean single series exists. Historical per-share BVPS is therefore NOT reconstructed from a fabricated historical share count -- year-over-year SHAREHOLDERS' EQUITY GROWTH is used as the proxy for BVPS growth in the historical_growth section (buybacks are confirmed immaterial: H1 2026 buybacks of ~$4.4B annualize to <1% of the ~$1.08T market cap and <1.2% of book value, so equity growth and BVPS growth are not meaningfully different). CURRENT shares outstanding (2,136.6M, B-share-equivalent) is a live-market input, not a historical guess: sourced from stockanalysis.com's live 'Shares Out: 2.14B' figure and cross-checked against market cap ($1.08T) / current price ($505.48) = 2,136.58M -- the two independent figures agree to within 0.01M, i.e. essentially exactly, so this is treated as reliable despite the historical XBRL gap. net_debt is held at 0: Berkshire's cash/T-bill pile and portfolio are inside book value, not a bridge adjustment, consistent with the 'never subtract net debt from an already-capitalized equity flow' rule for insurer/holdco models. inputs.last_fcf is deliberately omitted -- there is no owner-FCF concept in this model; the dashboard's generic toy-model fallback (used only for the slider RATIO, not the displayed default value) will be inert for this ticker, matching the FRFHF precedent for the same model family.
inputs.cash_and_equivalents_note: Q2 2026 balance-sheet 'cash and equivalents' line only ($40.6B) -- NOT the full ~$365.5B cash/T-bill pile disclosed qualitatively in Analysis JSON, which also includes short-term Treasury bills reported elsewhere on the balance sheet. Not used in the valuation: net_debt is held at 0 per the insurer/holdco convention (cash and securities are already inside book value, not a bridge adjustment).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr, blended toward the higher equity_3yr_cagr given the post-2023 acceleration and record retained capital base; used as the BASE case Year-1 BVPS growth rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue growth (0.6% 3yr CAGR, near-zero as insurance premium and industrial revenue plateaued FY2023-2025) diverges sharply from equity/BVPS growth (14.3% 3yr CAGR) -- this is EXPECTED and not a red flag for Berkshire: book value grows primarily from retained earnings, investment gains, and underwriting profit, not from revenue growth, since capital is redeployed into the securities portfolio and wholly-owned subsidiaries rather than driving reported top-line growth. Revenue CAGR is not a relevant proxy for this business and is recorded for completeness only.
historical_growth.notes: Equity growth used as the BVPS-growth proxy in place of a genuine per-share history, because current-year (2026) shares outstanding cannot be applied retroactively to book value from 2008-2025 without fabricating a historical share count the filings do not cleanly disclose (see inputs.notes). Buybacks have been small enough in most years (see kpis.buybacks) that equity growth and true BVPS growth are unlikely to differ by more than 1-2pp in any given year, and by materially less than the difference between scenarios.

base.description: BVPS compounds at a moderate 9.5% -> 8.0% glide, below the 10.1% 5yr and 14.3% 3yr realized CAGRs, reflecting Berkshire's sheer size (the 'elephant problem'), GEICO underwriting softening (pre-tax income -45% YoY Q2 2026), and a leadership transition to Abel whose capital-allocation record at this scale is unproven. Exit P/B of 1.35x sits mid-range of the post-2018 buyback-era trading band (~1.1x management buyback-comfort floor to ~1.6x), consistent with a normalized market view of Berkshire once the 'Buffett premium' uncertainty resolves either way.

bull.description: Abel deploys the $365-400B cash pile productively (large M&A, sustained net equity buying continuing the Q2 2026 pattern), GEICO underwriting recovers, and BHE's data-center power demand tailwind materializes, sustaining BVPS growth near the 3yr realized CAGR. Exit P/B 1.55x, near the top of the post-2018 range, reflecting a market that re-rates Berkshire once Abel's record is established and cash is seen as a strategic asset rather than a drag.

bear.description: The elephant problem bites: Abel cannot find acquisitions large enough to matter, the cash pile sits earning low money-market-like returns as rates fall, GEICO underwriting keeps deteriorating, and further loss of the 'Buffett premium' (Buffett, 95, further reduces involvement) compresses both growth and the multiple. Exit P/B 1.15x, just above the ~1.1x level management itself has signaled as a buyback-comfort floor, i.e. a level the market has approached but rarely sustained below for long.

sensitivity.row_axis: bvps_growth_rate_pct (avg of 5yr path, base path shifted uniformly)
sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows are the average annual BVPS growth rate (base 5-yr path [9.5,9.0,8.5,8.0,8.0]% shifted -4/-2/0/+2/+4pp uniformly, average shown in wacc_range field for dashboard-schema compatibility). Columns are the exit price-to-book multiple (1.05x-1.65x) applied to Year-5 BVPS, shown in terminal_growth_range field for the same reason. Cost of equity held fixed at the base case 8.5%. Field names retained from the owner-FCF schema for dashboard compatibility even though the axes here are BVPS growth and exit P/B, not WACC and perpetuity growth, per the insurer/holdco book-value-compounding methodology (see FRFHF precedent).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25. Bear held at the standard 25% (not lowered) despite Berkshire's balance-sheet strength, because the succession/key-man risk and GEICO underwriting deterioration are live, disclosed, and currently unfolding (not merely hypothetical downside), and because the bear case here is a growth/multiple problem, not a solvency problem -- appropriate weight, not a discount for improbability.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Berkshire Hathaway is valued as a book-value compounder, not a free-cash-flow business. Its GAAP operating cash flow and reported net income are dominated by insurance float placement, a >$300B T-bill portfolio, and mandatory mark-to-market swings on a large marketable-securities book (net income swung from -$22.8B in FY2022 to +$97.1B in FY2023 on investment marks alone) -- none of which is a meaningful proxy for the intrinsic value the business is creating year to year. This model instead (1) projects book value per share forward at a scenario-specific compounding rate derived from realized shareholders'-equity growth (14.3% 3yr, 10.1% 5yr, 10.8% 10yr CAGR), (2) applies a Year-5 exit price-to-book multiple drawn from Berkshire's own recent trading range (management has signaled comfort buying back stock near 1.1-1.2x book; the market has traded 1.3-1.6x in strong periods since the 2018 buyback-authorization change), and (3) discounts the resulting terminal value per share back to present at a cost of equity appropriate to a AAA-quality, permanent-capital conglomerate (7.5-10% across scenarios) -- there is no debt-funded capital structure or refinancing risk to price into a higher rate. No dividend is paid, so unlike a typical BVPS-compounding insurer (e.g. FRFHF), there is no interim distribution stream to discount and add; all scenario value sits in the terminal BVPS x exit-P/B leg. This mirrors the FRFHF (Fairfax) and NAB.AX approaches used elsewhere in this project for financial/holding companies where GAAP operating cash flow is not representative of distributable owner earnings.
key_risks_to_valuation: Succession/key-man risk: Greg Abel's capital-allocation record at Berkshire's scale is unproven; further reduction in Warren Buffett's (age 95) involvement as Chairman is a live, not hypothetical, risk over the projection horizon

GEICO underwriting deterioration (pre-tax underwriting income -45% YoY in Q2 2026 on rising bodily-injury claim frequency and severity) shows insurance results can swing quickly even absent catastrophe losses

The 'elephant problem': at a ~$1.08T market cap, few acquisitions are large enough to move results, risking a persistently low-yielding, growing cash pile if Abel cannot find attractive uses for capital

Exit-multiple risk is the dominant swing factor in this model (bear 1.15x to bull 1.55x drives most of the bear-to-bull value spread), and the multiple the market assigns Berkshire in 5 years is inherently a sentiment call, not a fundamental one, once Abel's tenure is established

Interest-income sensitivity: a large share of near-term earnings comes from ~$300-400B of T-bills; a falling-rate cycle reduces this income stream and could slow near-term BVPS growth below the projected path

Historical BVPS is a proxy (shareholders'-equity YoY growth), not a true reconstructed per-share series, because SEC XBRL share-count tags are unreliable for this dual-class filer after ~2011 -- see inputs.notes

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart), regular close per inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 464.01-537.74
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL via research/BRK-B/Reports/BRK-B.duckdb core_metrics (shareholders_equity FY2008-FY2025 and Q1/Q2 2026); kpis table (buybacks, cash_taxes, ebitda_da)
data_sources.shares_outstanding: stockanalysis.com live 'Shares Out' figure (2.14B), cross-checked against market cap / current price (independently computed, agrees to <0.01M); SEC XBRL dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding tag confirmed unreliable for this ticker post-2011 (Class A/B dimension collapse) and NOT used
data_sources.qualitative: research/BRK-B/Reports/BRK-B_Analysis.json (succession to Abel Jan 2026, GEICO underwriting softening, record cash pile, resumed buybacks, historical P/B trading range)

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
sanity_check.not_evaluated_reason: no rule had inputs: no annual row with revenue, equity or earnings on a known scale (core_metrics.units NULL? see make backfill-units) or no FY-end price aligned to it
